Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE AI 补全经历

Describe a person who often helps others

描述一个经常帮助他人的人

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a person who often helps others

  • Who this person is (这个人是谁)
  • How often he/she helps others (他/她多久帮一次他人)
  • How/why he/she helps others (他/她如何/为什么帮助他人)
  • And how you feel about this person (并谈谈你对这个人的感受)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a person who often helps others

I'd like to talk about a classmate of mine from university, who is probably the most helpful person I've ever met. He's in the same class as me, and everyone knows him as the guy you can always turn to. First of all, who he is: he's a student in my class, and we've studied together for a couple of years now. As for how often he helps others, it's honestly all the time. Before exams, he lends his notes to the whole class, and whenever someone has trouble installing software or setting up their computer, he's the first to offer a hand. The way he helps is what stands out most. He never makes you feel like you're bothering him, and he explains things patiently instead of just doing them for you. I remember once I was stuck on a homework problem, and he spent a whole evening going through it with me until I understood. He said he helps because he remembers how it feels to be confused, and he thinks helping others makes the whole class stronger. As for how I feel about him, I genuinely admire him. People like him are rare, because most of us are busy with our own stuff. Having him as a classmate has made my university life much easier, and honestly, he's inspired me to be more helpful to others too. So that's why I'd describe him as a person who truly cares about the people around him.

讲的是大学同班同学，是我见过最热心的人。他几乎随时都在帮人：考试前把笔记借给全班，有人装软件、弄电脑出问题他第一个帮忙。他帮人的方式最突出：从不让人觉得麻烦他，耐心讲解而不是直接代劳；有一次我作业卡住，他花了一整晚陪我弄懂。他说帮人是因为记得自己困惑时的感受，帮别人也让全班更强。我很佩服他，他让我也想变得更乐于助人。

Q2What can children do to help their parents?

Children can help their parents in quite simple ways. For example, they can do small household chores, like tidying their own room, washing dishes or taking out the rubbish. They can also help by being considerate, such as not making a mess and studying hard, which reduces their parents' worries. Even small gestures, like helping carry shopping bags, show that they care. I think the key is that the help doesn't need to be big, just consistent.

孩子帮父母的方式很简单：做小家务，比如整理自己房间、洗碗、倒垃圾；也可以懂事一点，不弄乱、认真学习，减少父母操心；甚至帮忙拎购物袋这样的小举动都能体现关心。关键不是帮多大忙，而是持续。

Q3Should children help their parents with household chores?

Yes, I think they should, and it's actually good for them. Doing chores teaches children responsibility and basic life skills that they'll need as adults, like cooking and cleaning. It also helps them understand how much work their parents do, which builds appreciation. Of course, the chores should be suitable for their age, but starting early is beneficial. In my view, children who help at home tend to grow up more independent and considerate.

应该帮，而且对孩子有好处。做家务教会孩子责任感和成年后需要的基本生活技能，比如做饭、打扫；也让他们理解父母有多辛苦，学会感恩。家务要适合年龄，但早点开始有益。在家帮忙的孩子长大后往往更独立、更体贴。

Q4What kind of help do people need when looking for a new job?

When people are job hunting, they need several kinds of help. Firstly, practical advice, like how to write a good CV and prepare for interviews. Secondly, connections, since many jobs are found through referrals from friends or former colleagues. They also need emotional support, because job hunting can be stressful and full of rejection. So I'd say the most valuable help combines information, connections and encouragement.

求职时需要几种帮助：一是实用建议，比如怎么写好简历、怎么准备面试；二是人脉，很多工作靠朋友或前同事推荐；三是情感支持，求职压力大、常被拒绝。最有价值的帮助是信息、人脉和鼓励的结合。

Q5Who should people ask for help, colleagues or family members?

I think it depends on the kind of help needed. For work-related problems, colleagues are usually the better choice, because they understand the situation and can give practical advice. Family members, on the other hand, are better for emotional support, since they care about you personally and are less likely to judge. So I'd say people should ask colleagues for professional help and family for personal support, rather than relying on only one side.

取决于需要什么帮助。工作上的问题找同事更好，因为他们了解情况、能给实用建议；情感支持找家人更好，因为他们真心关心你、不太会评判。所以专业问题问同事、个人问题问家人，不要只依赖一边。

Q6Do you think schools should teach children to do household chores?

I think it's a good idea, though it should be done in a light way. Schools could include simple life skills in their curriculum, like cooking, cleaning or basic repairs, because not every child learns these at home. This would help children become more independent and prepared for adult life. That said, schools shouldn't overload students with extra requirements, since they already have a heavy workload. So I'd support it as an optional or practical part of education.

好主意，但应该轻松地进行。学校可以在课程里加入简单生活技能，比如做饭、打扫、基础维修，因为不是每个孩子都在家学到这些；这能让孩子更独立、为成年生活做准备。但学校不该给学生加太多负担，他们课业已经很重。支持作为选修或实践部分。

Q7Why are employees reluctant to ask their managers for help?

I think the main reason is fear of looking incompetent. Many employees worry that asking for help will make their manager think they can't handle the job, which could hurt their chances of promotion. There's also the power gap, since in many workplaces, including mine, managers are seen as authority figures, which makes employees hesitate. And some managers are simply too busy or unapproachable. So the reluctance often comes from workplace culture rather than the employees themselves.

主要原因是怕显得无能：员工担心求助会让经理觉得自己干不了活，影响晋升机会。还有权力差距，很多职场里经理被视为权威人物，员工会犹豫；有些经理也确实太忙或不好接近。所以这种犹豫往往来自职场文化，而不是员工本身。
